name: payload-json-messages-untyped
hook: Conversations messages field stores opaque JSON without validation
body:
The `messages` field in Conversations collection is `type: 'json'` with no validation. Application code in `conversation-service.ts` defines the expected shape (role, content, timestamp, hidden, media, chatAssets). No compile-time or runtime enforcement exists.

Why: Storing untyped JSON means typos in message shape only surface at runtime in chat UI. Adding a Zod `validateBeforeChange` hook would catch malformed messages at write time.

How to apply: Before adding new JSON fields, define a Zod schema and add a `beforeChange` validation hook.

name: stringly-typed-select-fields
hook: Payload select fields (accessType, role) use string options without TypeScript union enforcement
body:
Several Payload collections use `type: 'select'` with string options (e.g., Courses.accessType: 'free'|'paid'|'mandatory'|'gated', Users.role: 'admin'|'editor'|'user'). TypeScript sees these as `string`, not the specific literal union.

Why: Callers switch on string values which only fail at runtime if a typo is made. The pattern is widespread in this codebase.

How to apply: Define a TypeScript union type matching the select options and add a `beforeChange` hook to validate the field value matches the union.

name: in-memory-rate-limit-serverless-broken
hook: In-memory Map rate limiter resets on serverless cold start
body:
rate-limit.ts uses `new Map()` for rate limit counters. On Vercel serverless (scale-to-zero), every new instance starts with an empty map, allowing users to bypass rate limits.

Why: Serverless functions don't share memory. Rate limit state must be persisted in MongoDB (already available as Payload/Mongoose).

How to apply: Use MongoDB atomic operations for rate limiting. Payload's Local API or raw Mongo driver can handle this.
